objective: Settle F10 before commit b: does the native path repopulate icon, version and description for an AppImage from its .desktop entry, with `calix-sync.py` never running -- so that `sync_appimages()` may be deleted?
verdict: Half. The harvest holds, the directory does not. The native path supplies the same metadata the Python does, but only for AppImages in the directory it scans, and that directory is not where this machine's AppImages are.

what_was_run.reproducer: .ci-cache/proof/f10-proof.sh (ignored scratch; the log is the durable record)
what_was_run.A: native `calix sync appimage --discover`, one AppImage in ~/.local/bin, desktop entry with Name/Comment/Icon/X-AppImage-Version -> 1 record carrying all four, Python never executed
what_was_run.B: same command, database deleted first, the AppImage in ~/Applications -> 0 records
what_was_run.C: the Python's `sync_appimages()` in the same scratch home, the same ~/Applications AppImage -> 1 record with the same fields
what_was_run.D: this machine read only: AppImageInstallPath null, 0 AppImages in ~/.local/bin, 15 in ~/Applications, 15 records, all under ~/Applications

why_it_matters.the_harvest_is_not_the_problem: discovery.zig reads the XDG desktop entries and builds name, version, icon and description from them, with filename fallbacks. It is wired into `calix sync appimage` (sync.zig:252) and merges without degrading a record: fields the filesystem cannot supply -- update URL and type, forge coordinates, prerelease opt-in, launch environment -- are carried over untouched, and records the scan does not see are kept rather than dropped.
why_it_matters.the_root_is: The native default is `xdg.binHome` (sync.zig:174, server.zig:319, install.zig:685) and the Python's is `~/Applications` (calix-sync.py:75). Each side is blind to the other's AppImages.
why_it_matters.consequence_for_the_daemon: Not the root. The daemon's `probeReleases` builds an `AppImageManager` with that directory but then reads `getAppImagesFromLocalDb()`, which opens `local_db_path` and nothing else, so the root never decides what is probed. `release-registry.json` is absent because every record in the live database carries `update_type: none` -- `probeReleases` skips an AppImage with no update source, so there is nothing for it to record. What the root does decide is whether the database is refreshed at all, and that is the part the cut would lose.
why_it_matters.consequence_for_the_database: The script's own comment records a previous implementation that "kept stale metadata forever". Cutting `sync_appimages()` while the native path scans an empty directory reproduces exactly that, deliberately.

plan_changed.S1 steps: Renumbered to 10. Step 6 records the verdict, new step 7 settles the roots with a red test first, step 8 deletes `sync_appimages()` in the same commit as the root it no longer supplies.
plan_changed.new_finding: F11 in the workstream document: two writers on one document (F10) and two disjoint scan roots (F11) are separate defects; fixing one does not fix the other.
plan_changed.proofs: F10's proof now states the two halves -- metadata supplied, and the root the AppImages are in -- instead of assuming one implies the other, plus a post-cut check that the database still advances with the script gone.

no_machine_change: Read-only on the host: the experiment wrote only under .ci-cache/, and case D only counted what is there. No unit changed, nothing deployed.

correction.what_was_wrong: The first version of this record, and the F11 row in the workstream document, said the absent `release-registry.json` was caused by the daemon probing `~/.local/bin`. It is not: the probe reads the database, not a directory.
correction.what_corrected_it: `getAppImagesFromLocalDb` opens `local_db_path` only (manager.zig:937), and the live database's fifteen records all carry `update_type: none`, which `probeReleases` skips by design.
correction.what_survives: The finding itself is untouched -- the native refresh does not see this machine's AppImages, so the Python is still the only thing refreshing the database, and cutting it without settling the root would freeze it.
